title: Sequenced routing resolver for gradual version rollouts and pinned model affinity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When a customer pins requests to a model version and we simultaneously run gradual rollouts (canary/weighted A-B) across multiple regions and capacity tiers, the current resolver sometimes produces counterintuitive fallbacks: a pinned request transiently routes to the canary variant in another region, or a low-tier request is promoted to a higher-cost variant due to routing precedence. This causes SLO blips and unexpected cost for customers that relied on pinning semantics.

Goal: Implement a sequenced routing resolver that enforces deterministic ordering between: (1) explicit model-version pinning, (2) rollout-affinity (percent/weight), (3) region preferences and availability, and (4) tier/capacity policies. The resolver must preserve pinning guarantees, support gradual traffic ramps for canaries, honor tier constraints, and fall back to compatible model variants only when strict constraints cannot be satisfied.

Scope: core routing decision logic for host-side request router and the control-plane policy that programs routing tables. Excludes UI changes in Console (separate PM ticket) and long-term policy language refactor (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Pinned requests always prefer the exact model version within the configured region set; pinning overrides rollout weight unless pin target is unavailable in all candidate endpoints.

When a pinned version is unavailable, resolver chooses fallback variants according to a deterministic chain: same region same-tier compatible variant -> same-region lower-tier with explicit downgrade policy -> cross-region same-tier -> cross-region lower-tier. Each step is recorded in logs and trace metadata.
Canary/A-B weighted routing only applies to non-pinned traffic and to pinned traffic explicitly opted into 'rollout-override' flag.
Tier constraints (dedicated vs shared) are always enforced; resolver must not promote shared-tier requests into dedicated pools unless explicit override and capacity permit it.
Integration tests covering: pin + canary coexistence; pin failure -> fallback chain; tier-respect under capacity pressure; cross-region fallback with latency penalty annotations.
Performance: resolver latency added at the router path <= 200 microseconds p95 in synthetic benchmark with 100k qps fanout (goal: 100 microseconds p95).
Telemetry: traces include decision steps (pin-check, rollout-eval, tier-check, fallback-step), and metrics emitted for pin-hits, pin-falls, rollout-redirects, and fallback-rate.
Operational playbook entry updated with steps to diagnose misrouted pinned traffic and safe rollback for rollout policies.
design_notes: Introduce a sequenced decision pipeline: 1) pin affinity check (hard/soft), 2) availability and health lookup, 3) rollout weight evaluation (only for eligible traffic), 4) tier/capacity constraint enforcement, 5) deterministic fallback chain builder.
Represent rollout affinity separately from pin affinity. Rollout affinity uses a stable hashing key (customer-id or request-id) and is applied only when pin affinity does not block it.
Add explicit 'pin-unavailable' reason codes so downstream can decide whether to surface an error or accept a fallback. Reasons: UNPROVISIONED, UNREGISTERED, DECOMMISSIONED, HEALTHY_BUT_OVER_CAPACITY.
Use a small in-memory cache for endpoint capability (version, tier, region) with TTL=30s to avoid extra control-plane calls. Cache must be invalidated on control-plane push events.
Keep the resolver deterministic and purely functional for a given inputs snapshot to make testing and replay easier.
implementation_plan: Core: implement SequencedRoutingResolver class in routing-service (runtime) with pipeline stages matching design notes.
Control-plane: extend policy API to publish 'variant-compatibility' metadata and explicit fallback chains for complex model families.
Router: add trace fields and structured log lines for each decision stage. Ensure logs are small (code + short reason) to avoid high cardinality.
Tests: unit tests for each stage, integration tests in the e2e harness simulating multi-region endpoints and tier failures.
Performance: microbenchmarks and `wrk`-style synthetic load tests; instrument resolver p95 and memory usage. Target optimization if p95 > 200us.
Docs: produce short design doc and update Routing operators guide with examples for pin+canary policy combos.
PRs: split into 3 PRs: resolver core, control-plane policy extension, router tracing + tests.
Deploy: staged rollout to staging cluster, then gradual canary in prod with full tracing enabled.
testing_plan: Unit: stage-level mocks for health/availability and rollout hash function to validate ordering and edge cases.
Integration: multi-region simulator (local) with 3 regions, 2 tiers; scenarios: pin-present, pin-absent, pinned-but-unavailable, capacity-pressure-induced fallback.
Chaos: kill endpoints to simulate regional outage and verify fallback chain and SLO behavior.
Regression: previous routing behavior must be replayable via a compatibility switch for 48 hours post-deploy to validate no customer regressions.
Load: 100k qps synthetic traffic with mixed pinned and unpinned distributions to ensure resolver overhead acceptable.
rollout_plan: Step 1 (staging): Deploy resolver and control-plane changes to staging and run integration harness for 48h.
Step 2 (canary in prod): Release to 5% of routers; monitor pin-hit ratio, fallback-rate, p95 latency for 24h.
Step 3 (ramp): 25% routers for next 24h if metrics stable; enable compatibility switch to fall back to old resolver within 10m.
Step 4 (full): 100% rollout and flip on default behavior; Keep old resolver available as hot rollback for 48h.
Observability: require full-traces and alerting on fallback-rate > 0.5% (baseline ~0.02%) or pin-hits drop > 5% relative to baseline.
telemetry: event: routing.decision.trace (structured span including stage timestamps and reason codes)
dashboard: Routing - Pin & Canary interplay, with filters for project, region, tier
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Resolver complexity causes increased request-latency. Mitigation: micro-optimized path for common-case (pin hit -> direct return), and cache endpoint capabilities.
Risk: High-cardinality trace fields. Mitigation: use small reason codes and sample traces for high-volume tenants.

Risk: Incorrect fallback semantics exposes customers to higher-cost models. Mitigation: enforce tier policy as hard constraint and add explicit approval step for cross-tier fallbacks in control-plane.
Risk: Rollout logic applied to pinned traffic unintentionally. Mitigation: default gating of rollout-affinity to non-pinned traffic and explicit 'rollout-override' opt-in flag for testing.
Risk: Coordination gap with Console/PM. Mitigation: link PM ticket and schedule a sync to ensure Console UI communicates the new semantics.
